cf.title: pg_stat_statements: fix SQL/JSON behavior keywords and JSON_TABLE query jumbling

input.subject: Re: pg_stat_statements replaces SQL/JSON ON EMPTY / ON ERROR keywords with parameters

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with examples, was reported on pgsql-bugs, and the remaining patch reuses the existing query_jumble_ignore node attributes. Michael Paquier committed the tests and the behavior keyword fix and limited the query ID change to master. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 9 messages are visible and no reply to v6 is shown.

brief.title: pg_stat_statements: jumble JSON_TABLE column definitions and keep SQL/JSON behavior keywords
brief.problem: pg_stat_statements merges JSON_TABLE queries that differ in column types, ON EMPTY or ON ERROR behaviors, NESTED PATH structure or PLAN join types, because TableFunc.colvalexprs and TableFunc.plan are not jumbled. It also replaced behavior keywords such as TRUE or EMPTY with parameter symbols, so separate entries showed the same text. Users who monitor SQL/JSON queries get wrong or confusing entries.
brief.proposed_design: The behavior keyword fix leaves the behavior Const without a location; Michael Paquier committed it. The remaining patch includes TableFunc.colvalexprs and TableFunc.plan in query jumbling and gives NESTED PATH Consts their literal location so they show as parameter symbols. JsonExpr.column_name and JsonTablePath.name are marked query_jumble_ignore, so column names and path names stay out of the query ID.
user_visible_surface: Query IDs of JSON_TABLE queries change on master.
Query IDs of other SQL/JSON query functions change, since their NULL column_name is no longer jumbled.
pg_stat_statements normalized text shows NESTED PATH and column path literals as parameter symbols.
pg_stat_statements normalized text keeps ON EMPTY and ON ERROR keywords (committed part).
author_claims: Everything left in the jumbled plan nodes affects the query result.
Equivalent PLAN spellings, such as no PLAN and PLAN (p0 OUTER p1), still share a query ID.
Queries that differ only in column names, path names, or PATH after NESTED stay merged.
Ignoring column names matches how column definition lists of functions in FROM are handled.
The series applies to master and REL_19_STABLE and passes tests on both.
brief.thread_state: Michael Paquier committed the new sqljson.sql tests and the behavior keyword fix, and ruled out any back-patch. v6 adopts Sami Imseih's request to ignore column names; no reply to v6 is visible.
unclear: No reviewer has yet commented on jumbling TableFunc.plan, which Sami Imseih earlier found hard to accept.
The split between "a jsonb PATH" and "a jsonb FORMAT JSON PATH" was left as is; no reviewer has accepted it.
The thread does not say whether ignoring the name of a column without PATH merges columns that read different keys, and whether reviewers accept that.
The committed tests miss items Michael Paquier listed, such as WITHOUT UNIQUE and JSON_ARRAYAGG ORDER BY; the thread does not say whether they were added.
search_queries: normalized query text keyword replaced parameter

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes jumble attributes of TableFunc, JsonExpr and JsonTablePath in primnodes.h, so query IDs seen by extensions change.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Query IDs of JSON_TABLE and other SQL/JSON query functions change, so Michael Paquier ruled out a back-patch in message #2.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Future fields added to JsonTablePathScan or JsonTableSiblingJoin are jumbled by default and need a decision each time.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Do reviewers accept jumbling TableFunc.plan with the fields listed in message #1, which Sami Imseih earlier found hard to get comfortable with?
Is it accepted that COLUMNS (a int) and COLUMNS (b int) now share one entry, although they read different keys?
Should "a jsonb PATH" and "a jsonb FORMAT JSON PATH" keep separate query IDs, and which reviewer has agreed to that?
Were tests for WITHOUT UNIQUE and JSON_ARRAYAGG ORDER BY, which Michael Paquier listed, added to sqljson.sql?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier, who knows query jumbling and pg_stat_statements, reviewed the series and committed the tests and the behavior keyword fix.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the query ID change of all SQL/JSON query functions in the next major version, and for the jumble attributes on the JSON_TABLE plan nodes from then on.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered each review within days and posted v3 through v6, adopting the reviewers' requests each time.

priority.reason: Only users who monitor JSON_TABLE queries with pg_stat_statements benefit, but their entries are wrong today. The remaining patch is about 20 KiB, mostly expected test output, touches two source files, and a committer who knows the area is engaged.

provisional_note: Without the code, it could not be checked that every jumbled field of the JSON_TABLE plan nodes affects the result, or that the new NESTED PATH Const locations match the literals. The discussion in messages #4 to #9 was not visible.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Query Jumbling for CALL and SET utility statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made pg_stat_statements compute a query ID by jumbling CALL and SET statements, so calls that differ only in constants share one entry. This was meant to cut LWLock contention under track_utility; later versions added 2PC and savepoint commands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found no clear reason to jumble some utility statements and not others, and preferred jumbling all of them with code generated from the node definitions. Michael Paquier also worried about the cost of jumbling frequent transaction commands. The thread then stalled, and he returned the patch because the generated-code approach did not exist yet.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So, this thread has stalled for the last few weeks and it seems to me that the conclusion is that we'd want an approach using a set of scripts that automate the generation of the code in charge of the DDL jumbling.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_stat_statements query jumbling to use relation name instead of relation oid
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Julien Rouhaud, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_stat_statements query jumbling to hash the relation name instead of the relation OID, so a queryid stays the same after a table is dropped and re-created. The author wanted stable, name-based queryids for use in other extensions such as pgaudit and sql_firewall.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan opposed the change, since renaming a table does not make it a different table. Julien Rouhaud and Michael Paquier noted that the patch ignores the schema (and the database), and that renames would change the queryid. Tom Lane said the idea only works if every OID in the jumble (types, operators, functions) is replaced by a name, and that the extra name lookups could cost much performance, so he voted to reject.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That argument would only hold if *every* use of OIDs in the jumbles
were replaced by names --- not only tables, but types, operators,
functions, etc.  I'm already concerned that the additional name
lookups will cost a lot of performance, and I think adding so many
more would probably be disastrous.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PROPOSAL] : Disallow use of empty column name in (column_name '') in ALTER or CREATE of foreign table.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw's validator reject empty values for the column_name, schema_name and table_name options in create or alter foreign table. Today an empty column_name is accepted, and the remote query then fails with a zero-length identifier error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane judged that the check did not add enough ease-of-use to justify the extra code, and he compared an empty name to a misspelled remote name, which cannot be checked either. Robert Haas pointed out that existing foreign tables with empty values would then fail pg_dump or pg_upgrade. Nobody argued for the patch after Tom voted against it, so Robert marked it Rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I was down on it to start with, on the grounds that it wasn't adding enough ease-of-use to justify even a relatively small amount of added code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sampling of queries in pg_stat_statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_statements.sample_rate setting so pg_stat_statements records statistics for only a fraction of queries, which lowers its overhead under high load. Later versions moved the sampling check into pgss_enabled() and set the per-query sampling decision in pgss_post_parse_analyze().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not say why the author withdrew the entry, one day after posting it. The only reservation came from Michael Paquier, who did not want to add sampling before studying the actual bottlenecks. He suggested moving pg_stat_statements into the central pgstats with the custom APIs, which would remove the query text file and shrink the hash key, but he did not plan that work for PG18.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: FWIW, I'm not eager to integrate this proposal without looking at this exact argument in depth.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extracting only the columns needed for a query
precedents_retrieved.summary: Have the planner compute, for each relation in a query, the set of columns that actually need to be scanned (a scanCols bitmap stored in RangeTblEntry, extracted in make_one_rel()), so table access methods such as zedstore can use it for costing and execution. Companion patches showed an extended ANALYZE API and a per-column disk-size statistic for using scanCols in cost estimation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The authors withdrew the entry themselves. They said they would post a new thread with a combined patch set: the scanCols patch, a patch to capture RETURNING columns, and patches passing the column list to table AM functions. Review had also found open issues, such as excess scanCols for DELETE ... USING ... RETURNING and for partitioned tables, which the authors said were tricky to fix within the current extraction logic. No reviewer objected to the approach.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Melanie and me will be posting a separate thread with the scanCols patch
listed here, a patch to capture the set of cols in RETURNING and a group
of patches to pass down the list of cols to various table AM functions
together as a patch set.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_stat_statements display of normalized FETCH counts
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a query_normalized flag to pgssEntry, so a FETCH with a count can replace an unnormalized query text stored earlier by a FETCH without a count. A new pgss_store() parameter limits this replacement to FETCH, because SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION would break otherwise.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier said the expectation was wrong: both FETCH forms jumble to the same node once howMany is ignored, and pg_stat_statements keeps the first query string it sees. He also rejected the extra generate_normalized_query() call because it makes pg_stat_statements heavier. He named a new FetchDirectionKeywords value in gram.y as the right fix if the two forms ever need to be told apart, but saw no monitoring gain. The author then withdrew the patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optionally record Plan IDs to track plan changes for a query
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds an optional in-core plan ID, controlled by a new compute_plan_id GUC, computed by hashing plan nodes during the setrefs.c tree walk and shown in pg_stat_activity, EXPLAIN and auto_explain. A pg_stat_plans contrib extension, built on the extensible cumulative statistics system, records per-plan statistics and the first plan text as an example consumer.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier judged that the planner's internals make a strict definition of what the plan hash covers hard to set down, and he did not expect the core plan ID and pg_stat_plans patches before the next release freeze. Which plan node fields to jumble was still open, and reviewers wanted node attributes in place of the custom JumblePlanNode() logic. A proposed rename of the jumbling code drew a -1 from Alvaro Herrera, so only parts of the preparatory work went in.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The intrisincs of the planner make putting a strict definition of what a hash means hard to set down, we should work towards studying that more first.  I don't see this happen until the next release freeze.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq compression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds streaming compression of libpq traffic with zlib or zstd, chosen at build time and enabled by a compression connection option, as a replacement for deprecated SSL compression. A compression layer wraps the socket read and write calls in both backend and frontend and passes tx/rx functions into the compression stream.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected to the design: the compression option sent in the startup packet, and the compression stream bypassing secure_read()/pqsecure_read() rather than working as a layer under them, which they found invasive. The author and reviewers did not reach consensus on this layering, and Dmitry Dolgov posted an alternative experimental patch. In the last commitfest the patch had failing tests and no review, and the visible messages do not show a closing statement.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have not actually looked much at your patch, but I am wondering if it could not be possible to make the whole footprint less invasive which really worries me as now shaped.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
Reverted commit(s): JSON_TABLE PLAN clause
precedents_retrieved.objection:
86ab7f4c721d commit made the table-level ON ERROR clause serve as the default
ON ERROR for columns lacking their own, so that a top-level ERROR ON ERROR
turned per-column evaluation errors into hard errors.

The SQL standard does mandate this cascade, but introducing it should be
a deliberate, separately-documented change, so restore the previous
behavior for now.  This also reverts the paired ruleutils.c logic that
deparsed a column's behavior against an ERROR default: that dropped an
explicit ERROR ON EMPTY from a dumped view, and otherwise emitted a
redundant NULL ON EMPTY.

precedents_retrieved.title: In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
Reverted commit(s): Fix corner case for a BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger returning OLD.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Previously, ExecInitModifyTable relied on ExecInitJunkFilter,
and thence ExecCleanTypeFromTL, to build the target descriptor from
the query tlist.  While we just checked (in ExecCheckPlanOutput)
that the tlist produces compatible output, this is not a great
substitute for the relation's actual tuple descriptor that's
available from the relcache.  For one thing, dropped columns will
not be correctly marked attisdropped; it's a bit surprising that
we've gotten away with that this long.  But the real reason for
being concerned with this is that using the table's descriptor means
that the slot will have correct attrmissing data, allowing us to
revert the klugy fix of commit ba9f18abd.  (This commit undoes
that one's changes in trigger.c, but keeps the new test case.)
Thus we can solve the bogus-trigger-tuple problem with fewer cycles
rather than more.

No back-patch, since this doesn't fix any additional bug, and it
seems somewhat more likely to have unforeseen side effects than
ba9f18abd's narrow fix.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P7] dealt with FETCH count normalization, and its reason (both forms jumble to the same node, no monitoring gain) does not apply, because the JSON_TABLE fields jumbled here change query results. [P2] proposed hashing relation names instead of OIDs, a different idea. The thread points to no earlier attempt at JSON_TABLE jumbling.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. The patch adds no syntax, keyword, GUC, catalog object or psql change. Query ID changes are limited to master and stated in the commit message, and Michael Paquier ruled out a back-patch in messages #2 and #4. Ignoring column names follows the column definition lists of functions in FROM (message #7). The author first argued that columns without PATH read different keys (message #1), then accepted ignoring the names in message #9, so the point is settled in the thread. The FORMAT JSON split matches existing JSON_QUERY behavior. [P2] and [P7] do not apply: neither recorded reason concerns jumbling fields that affect query results.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state. It changes query jumbling and Const locations, which feed only in-memory query IDs and pg_stat_statements text; no catalog, WAL, on-disk or wire change, and master-only, so query ID consistency between a primary and a standby on the same major version holds.

The proposal changes only which JSON_TABLE parse-tree fields go into the query ID and which Consts get a text location. It adds no privilege, role, function or setting, and it does not change who can read pg_stat_statements or what entries show beyond normalized constants. Literals still become parameter symbols, so query texts expose no new values.

No maintenance or fit objection holds. The change reuses the existing node-attribute jumbling, touches no hot path for non-users, and adds jumbling cost only to JSON_TABLE queries. Michael Paquier, who knows this area, committed the tests and the keyword fix, and the query ID change is limited to master, which Michael Paquier required in messages #2 and #4. Open design questions (TableFunc.plan, the FORMAT JSON split) belong to other angles.

The proposal fixes query jumbling inside pg_stat_statements' own query ID computation. No existing feature, setting or extension can make JSON_TABLE column definitions part of the query ID, and compute_query_id = off with an external jumbler would replace the mechanism, not reuse it. The patch extends the existing node-attribute jumbling, so it adds no second mechanism.

No demand objection. pg_stat_statements merges JSON_TABLE queries that differ in column types, behaviors or PLAN join types, so entries are wrong; this was reported on pgsql-bugs and two reviewers and a committer engaged. Costs fall on master only, where query IDs already change across major versions, and neither [P7] nor [P2] has a recorded reason that applies.
